answer: A staking bond makes each identity expensive: an agent must lock collateral before it can earn, so spawning thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of bonds. Like shale that only yields oil after costly drilling, an island registry that admits members only after a verifiable work deposit, or a meadow where every grazing plot needs its own fence, the bond turns cheap duplication into a priced resource. Attackers can still buy identities, but the cost scales linearly with each fake, while an honest agent pays once.
